core.title: Plan comparison and billing management
covers: confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions
core.guidance: Plans are a radio group of equal-width cards with the current plan marked in text (not colour only), prices with tabular figures and the billing period stated, a feature list with real text (no bare check marks without labels), and one primary action per state (Upgrade / Downgrade / Current); every card is one Tab stop with a visible focus ring, arrow keys move between plans; seat management is a data table (name, role, status, last active) with row actions reachable from the keyboard and a bulk selection state; invoice history is a table with date, amount (tabular), status text + icon and a real download link (not a hover-only icon); plan changes and seat removals confirm in a dialog that states the billing consequence and returns focus; billing settings sub-navigation is a vertical list with aria-current.
core.use_when: Billing/plan pages: choosing or changing a plan, seat management, invoice history, payment method.
core.avoid_when: Public pricing marketing pages (hero + narrative) or checkout for a one-off purchase.

implementation.nextjs: Server component for the invoice table; client radio group for plans; shadcn Dialog with returnFocus; Table with <th scope> and numeric cells using tabular-nums.
implementation.react: role=radiogroup on the plan row; roving tabindex; download as <a download> with the file name in the link text.

core.title: Bordered cards
core.guidance: Border token with measured contrast, 6–8 px radius, header row with title and one action, body with a clear hierarchy; selectable cards (plans) use a stronger border + check mark, never colour alone.
core.use_when: Settings pages, integration lists, plan pickers: discrete objects on a light canvas where a 1 px border (≥3:1) delineates without elevation.
core.avoid_when: Nested inside other cards or panels; on dark themes where borders vanish (use tonal steps).

core.title: Settings screen
covers: settings grouped with visible current values
confirmation of destructive or high-risk actions
core.guidance: Grouped rows with clear labels and current values visible, toggles for booleans with immediate effect, pickers for enums, destructive actions at the end with confirmation, search for long settings, platform idiom (grouped lists on mobile, sections/panes on desktop, TV: vertical list with DPAD and a right-side value column). Save behaviour explicit (auto vs Save button).
core.avoid_when: Never bury frequently changed settings three levels deep; never use toggles for actions.
core.selected_for: required coverage: settings grouped with visible current values

guardrails.title: Everything operable by keyboard, no traps
guardrails.guidance: Tab reaches every control in visual order; composite widgets use arrow keys with a roving tabindex so Tab is not consumed by every cell; Escape closes layers and returns focus to the invoker; nothing traps focus except a modal, and the modal itself must be escapable. Provide a keyboard alternative for every drag interaction.
guardrails.use_when: Every interactive element, including custom widgets, drag/drop, sliders, menus, date pickers, and anything that appears on hover.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: accessibility, interaction, no hover dependence, keyboard navigation and focus order

guardrails.title: Oversized display text and 'big number' KPIs everywhere
covers: visual hierarchy with one focal point
guardrails.guidance: Reserve display sizes for one element per screen; app headings 20–28 px; KPI value 24–32 px with a readable label; hierarchy comes from contrast between roles, not from making everything large. TV is the exception with its own scale.
guardrails.use_when: 72–96 px headlines on app screens, KPI tiles with 48 px numbers and tiny labels, everything bold.
guardrails.avoid_when: A single large focal number is fine when it is the screen's one thing.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: anti-pattern, visual hierarchy with one focal point

guardrails.title: Focus visible and not obscured
guardrails.guidance: Focus indicator ≥2 px with ≥3:1 contrast against adjacent colours and against the unfocused state; sticky UI gets scroll-padding so a focused control scrolls into clear view. On TV the indicator must be obvious at 3 m (scale + border/glow).
guardrails.use_when: Every focusable element in every theme; sticky headers, footers, toasts, and cookie banners must never cover the focused element.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never remove focus styles; use :focus-visible to hide them for mouse clicks only.

guardrails.title: Spacing from one scale, grouping by proximity
guardrails.guidance: A geometric-ish scale (4/8/12/16/24/32/48/64), inside-group spacing smaller than between-group spacing (ratio ≥1.5×), alignment to a grid, consistent inset per container type, optical alignment for icons and text baselines. Inconsistent spacing is the most common 'unprofessional' signal.
guardrails.use_when: Every layout decision; every 'spacing feels off' complaint.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never use arbitrary values (13px, 22px); never use equal spacing everywhere (kills grouping).

guardrails.title: Design empty, loading, error, and partial states
guardrails.guidance: Empty: what this is, why it is empty, one action. Loading: skeleton with final dimensions, then content; announce completion. Error: what failed, what to do, retry that works; keep entered data. Partial: show what loaded, mark what didn't. On TV, focus must land somewhere valid in each state.
guardrails.use_when: Every list, table, chart, form, and detail screen.
guardrails.avoid_when: Never ship a blank area for empty data; never show a spinner for more than ~1 s without a skeleton or progress; never show an error without a next step.
guardrails.selected_for: required coverage: loading, empty and error states
